tools_used: courtlistener MCP search (rate-limited, no data returned)
helpful: The provisioned petition text with a separate questions-presented cut; the split and vehicle sections were the core of the forecast.
The sal-v4 segment table's bracketed reached figures, which made the band anchor a two-line computation.
gaps: CourtListener MCP returned HTTP 429 (300/hour) on the first call of the cell, so the fan-out appears to share one rate-limit bucket; a per-cell budget or a cached docket read for the case's own live docket would have let me confirm the related-docket identities and check for a post-snapshot response request.

fedcourts query has no filter that reaches a doctrinal topic on SCOTUS rows (topic is circuit-only), so era/disposition queries return recency-ranked applications rather than comparable cert petitions.
A pre-computed grant rate for waived-response paid petitions with no response request would be a sharper anchor than the band mean for this very common shape.
notes: The petition is 120 pages and truncated; the appended Sixth Circuit opinion and district court order were only partly readable. One MCP retry after writing the drafts also returned HTTP 429.
